claims: Artemis II is scheduled for 2026.
Artemis II is a first-crewed flight test of NASA’s Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II is a first-crewed flight test of NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis II has a duration of approximately 10 days.
Artemis II will carry four astronauts around the Moon and back.
Artemis II will verify all spacecraft systems—including life support—in deep space.
The primary purpose of Artemis II is testing the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems with a crew on board.
The primary purpose of Artemis II is testing the Orion spacecraft's navigation systems with a crew on board.
The primary purpose of Artemis II is testing the Orion spacecraft's propulsion systems with a crew on board.
Artemis II will take four astronauts on a free-return trajectory around the Moon.
The Artemis II trajectory reaches up to 252,760 miles from Earth.
The Artemis II trajectory comes within roughly 4,000 miles of the lunar surface.
Astronauts will manually operate the Orion spacecraft on Artemis II.
Astronauts will test the Orion spacecraft on Artemis II.
Artemis II involves conducting in-flight human health studies.
Artemis II includes crew from NASA and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).
The Artemis II crew is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA).
Artemis II is the first crewed Artemis mission.
Artemis II is the first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
Artemis II will launch from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
Artemis II will launch on the SLS rocket.
The Artemis II trajectory includes a translunar injection.
The Artemis II trajectory circles the Moon.
Artemis II will return for a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
